ITALY’S FERTILITY RATE COLLAPSE (1950–2025)
Italy is experiencing one of the most severe demographic declines in the developed world.
Here’s the graphic showing the dramatic drop in Italy’s total fertility rate over the past 75 years:
Chart Description (attach this chart):
•  A clean line or bar chart showing Italy’s fertility rate falling from 2.5 children per woman in 1950 to just 1.2 in 2025.
•  The steepest decline happened between 1970 and 1995.
•  Current rate is far below the 2.1 replacement level needed to sustain a population.
Key Takeaways:
•  Italy recorded only ~355,000 births in 2025 — the lowest number since the country was founded in 1861.
•  Deaths now far outnumber births, leading to rapid population aging and shrinkage.
•  Without high immigration, Italy’s population would be declining even faster.
This is a slow-motion crisis that threatens Italy’s economy, workforce, pensions, and long-term future.
